annotations.description: Blocking Reality Smasher (5/5 with trample) with Phelia (2/2) is a poor trade. Phelia dies, and trample still deals 3 damage through. Phelia is a high-value creature that generates card advantage through her exile/flicker ability and is key to the Death & Taxes strategy. By blocking, KimiK2 loses Phelia to save only 2 life (taking 3 trample damage instead of 5). Additionally, Phelia could have been protected by not blocking and instead used on future attacks to exile opponent's threats like Chalice of the Void or Reality Smasher itself. The player also has Pre-War Formalwear in hand which could bring Phelia back, but that's a 3-mana investment that could be used more efficiently. Taking 5 damage (going to 15) while keeping Phelia on board would have been significantly better than losing this key creature to save 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Reality Smasher with Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd, losing Phelia and still taking 3 trample damage.
annotations.betterLine: Don't block. Take 5 damage (going to 15 life), keep Phelia alive to attack next turn and exile Reality Smasher or Chalice of the Void, generating significant tempo advantage.

annotations.description: Casting Stoneforge Mystic for mana when Aether Vial has 2 charge counters and could put SFM onto the battlefield for free. By casting SFM, they spend 2 mana and can't also cast Pre-War Formalwear (costs 3) this turn. Using Vial for SFM would leave all lands untapped to cast Formalwear, which would reanimate Phelia from the graveyard - a much more powerful turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Stoneforge Mystic using mana, consuming 2 of their 4 available mana
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Vial (at 2 counters) to put Stoneforge Mystic onto the battlefield for free, search for an equipment with SFM's ETB, then use the 4 available mana to cast Pre-War Formalwear to reanimate Phelia from the graveyard

annotations.description: KimiK2 Vorthos declined to activate Aether Vial (which has charge counters on it) during their precombat main phase. With Stoneforge Mystic already on board, they could use Stoneforge's activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}) to put Batterskull directly onto the battlefield, which would create a 4/4 vigilance lifelink Germ token — excellent against Reality Smasher. However, even without that line, declining to use Aether Vial's free creature deployment ability is leaving value on the table. The Vial activation is a pure upside free ability that costs no mana. Additionally, they skipped their attack phase with Stoneforge Mystic available (though attacking into Reality Smasher would be poor). The key miss is not using Stoneforge Mystic's ability to put Batterskull onto the battlefield this turn — Scrubland provides {W}, and between Scrubland and other lands they should have access to {1}{W} to activate Stoneforge. With Batterskull on the field, the 4/4 lifelink token would help stabilize against Reality Smasher significantly.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate Aether Vial and passed without deploying any threats or using Stoneforge Mystic's ability to cheat Batterskull into play.
annotations.betterLine: Use Stoneforge Mystic's activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}) to put Batterskull onto the battlefield, creating a 4/4 vigilance lifelink Germ token to stabilize against Reality Smasher. The lands available (Scrubland untapped) could provide the mana needed, though Karakas and Wasteland appear tapped. If mana is insufficient for Stoneforge activation, at minimum activate Aether Vial to deploy any matching creature from hand for free.

annotations.description: Playing Ancient Tomb as the land drop instead of Eye of Ugin loses significant tempo. Eye of Ugin reduces colorless Eldrazi costs by 2, enabling casting both Glaring Fleshraker (effectively 1 mana) and Thought-Knot Seer (effectively 2 mana) in the same turn for only 3 of the 4 available mana. Ancient Tomb only provides 6 total mana, insufficient to cast both (7 mana needed). This misses deploying an extra creature and the Fleshraker triggers.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to play Ancient Tomb as the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Eye of Ugin as land drop (sacrificing City of Traitors), then cast Glaring Fleshraker for 1 mana and Thought-Knot Seer for 2 mana, deploying two creatures and stripping opponent's hand while generating Fleshraker triggers.

annotations.description: Playing Eye of Ugin as the land drop sacrifices City of Traitors (which produces {C}{C}), replacing it with Eye of Ugin (which only produces {C} via tap, or provides a cost reduction for colorless Eldrazi spells). The player loses 2 colorless mana production this turn. With City of Traitors + Ancient Tomb + Cavern of Souls + Lotus Petal, the player had 7 mana available (2+2+1+1 from lands, plus Lotus Petal for 1) and could cast Thought-Knot Seer (costs 3C = 4 mana) before playing the land. After sacrificing City of Traitors to Eye of Ugin, the available mana drops significantly. The player could have cast Thought-Knot Seer first using City of Traitors mana, THEN played Eye of Ugin. With Eye of Ugin's cost reduction, they might have even been able to cast a second creature. Instead, by playing Eye of Ugin first, they lose City of Traitors' mana before using it, significantly reducing what they can deploy this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Eye of Ugin as land drop first, sacrificing City of Traitors before tapping it for mana.
annotations.betterLine: Tap City of Traitors for {C}{C} first, then cast Thought-Knot Seer (using City of Traitors + Ancient Tomb + Cavern of Souls for 4+ mana), then play Eye of Ugin. This would allow deploying TKS to strip a card from opponent's hand while still getting Eye of Ugin onto the battlefield. With Eye of Ugin's cost reduction, could potentially also cast Glaring Fleshraker with remaining mana.

annotations.description: Blocking Reality Smasher (5/5 with trample) with Stoneforge Mystic (1/2) is a terrible trade. Stoneforge Mystic dies, 4 trample damage still gets through (so only 1 damage is prevented), and KimiK2 loses their most important creature — the one that can cheat Batterskull into play for just 1W. Stoneforge Mystic with Batterskull in hand is an incredibly valuable piece that should not be thrown away to prevent 1 point of damage. Without Stoneforge, they'll need to hardcast Batterskull for 5 mana, which is much slower and may not happen against the Eldrazi pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Reality Smasher with Stoneforge Mystic
annotations.betterLine: Don't block. Take 5 damage (going to 12 life) and preserve Stoneforge Mystic to activate next turn, putting Batterskull onto the battlefield for 1W. The lifelink from Batterskull would quickly recover the life lost and stabilize the board.

annotations.description: With Eye of Ugin reducing costs by 2, Glaring Fleshraker costs just 1 mana and Thought-Knot Seer costs just 2 mana. Casting Fleshraker first, then TKS, would net an extra Eldrazi Spawn token and 1 damage to opponent from Fleshraker's triggers. Casting TKS first (or alone) misses these synergy triggers.
annotations.actionTaken: Appears to have chosen Thought-Knot Seer as the first/only cast, missing Fleshraker synergy triggers.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Glaring Fleshraker first (1 mana with Eye discount), then cast Thought-Knot Seer (2 mana) to trigger Fleshraker's abilities, creating a Spawn token and dealing 1 damage to opponent.

annotations.description: KimiK2 Vorthos declined to activate Wasteland during their upkeep, missing the opportunity to destroy a key nonbasic land like Eye of Ugin (which reduces Eldrazi costs by 2) or Ancient Tomb (which provides 2 colorless mana). Eye of Ugin is particularly important to destroy as it makes all of the opponent's Eldrazi spells significantly cheaper. The opponent has a Reality Smasher already in play and Eye of Ugin will continue to enable undercosted Eldrazi threats. Additionally, Aether Vial should have been activated to put a charge counter on it during upkeep - though looking at the choices, only Aether Vial activate and Wasteland activate are offered. The Aether Vial trigger happens automatically at beginning of upkeep, so that's separate. The key miss is declining to use Wasteland to destroy Eye of Ugin, which is a powerful cost-reduction land that will continue generating advantage for the Eldrazi player.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to activate any abilities during upkeep, passing priority without using Wasteland.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting Eye of Ugin to destroy the opponent's cost-reduction land, significantly slowing down their ability to deploy cheap Eldrazi threats.

annotations.description: KimiK2 cast White Orchid Phantom before playing the Wasteland from hand. Playing the land first is free and provides an additional Wasteland activation to destroy a second nonbasic land from the opponent (who relies heavily on nonbasic lands like Eye of Ugin, Ancient Tomb, and Cavern of Souls). The creature could still be cast afterward with the same mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast White Orchid Phantom before playing Wasteland from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Wasteland from hand first, then cast White Orchid Phantom. This preserves the option to activate both Wastelands to destroy two of opponent's critical nonbasic lands.

annotations.description: White Orchid Phantom's ETB is being used to destroy Eye of Ugin. While Eye of Ugin provides a cost reduction for colorless Eldrazi spells and a tutor ability, the opponent already has a Reality Smasher on board and Ancient Tomb still provides 2 colorless mana. Destroying Ancient Tomb would cut off the opponent's primary colorless mana source (2 mana per tap), making it much harder to cast future Eldrazi threats. Eye of Ugin only produces mana via its expensive 7-mana tutor activation and provides a 2-mana discount on Eldrazi spells, but with City of Traitors already in the graveyard and only Cavern of Souls + Ancient Tomb as mana sources, removing Ancient Tomb would be more crippling to the opponent's ability to cast spells at all. However, Eye of Ugin's cost reduction is powerful for chaining Eldrazi, so this is debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Destroyed Eye of Ugin with White Orchid Phantom's ETB trigger
annotations.betterLine: Destroying Ancient Tomb would remove the opponent's primary source of colorless mana production (2 mana per tap), leaving them with only Cavern of Souls for mana. This would be more devastating to the opponent's ability to cast future threats, as Eye of Ugin's cost reduction matters less if they can't generate enough total mana.

annotations.description: Pre-War Formalwear's ETB lets you return a creature with MV 3 or less from graveyard. The choice is between Phelia (2/2 flash, flickers permanents on attack) and Stoneforge Mystic (1/2, tutors equipment and cheats it in). KimiK2 already has Batterskull in hand, so Stoneforge's ETB tutor is less critical, but Stoneforge's activated ability ({1}{W}, {T}: put an Equipment from hand onto battlefield) would let them cheat Batterskull into play for just 1W instead of paying 5 mana. With all lands tapped this turn, neither creature can activate immediately, but Stoneforge would enable putting Batterskull into play next turn for just 1W (requiring only 2 mana), whereas without Stoneforge they need 5 mana for Batterskull. Phelia with Pre-War Formalwear becomes a 4/4 flash flier that can flicker things on attack, which is strong, but the opponent has Reality Smasher (5/5 trample haste) threatening lethal pressure. Getting Batterskull (4/4 vigilance lifelink germ) into play cheaply via Stoneforge seems more impactful for stabilizing at 14 life against a 5/5 trampler. However, Phelia could potentially flicker the opponent's Reality Smasher or Chalice of the Void, which has value too. The Aether Vial in hand is also dead due to Chalice on 0 countering it when cast — wait, Chalice is on 0 counters, and Aether Vial costs 1, so actually Aether Vial can be cast. This is debatable but Stoneforge enabling cheap Batterskull deployment seems stronger for the current board state.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Phelia, Exuberant Shepherd as the creature to return with Pre-War Formalwear
annotations.betterLine: Choose Stoneforge Mystic to return, enabling cheating Batterskull into play next turn for just 1W, providing a 4/4 vigilance lifelink body to stabilize against Reality Smasher pressure

annotations.description: Eldrazi Linebreaker costs {1}{C}{R}, requiring red mana. Cavern of Souls (chosen type: Eldrazi) can produce colored mana only for Eldrazi creature spells, so it can produce {R} for Linebreaker. However, casting Linebreaker consumes both Ancient Tombs (one tapped, one used for mana) and the Lotus Petal, leaving no mana to also cast Thought-Knot Seer this turn. Thought-Knot Seer (4/4) would strip a card from the opponent's hand, which is very valuable when the opponent has Aether Vial active and likely holding creatures like Phelia or other threats. Linebreaker's combat trigger gives +X/+0 where X is number of Eldrazi you control - with just Linebreaker and Reality Smasher, that's +2/+0 to one creature. Reality Smasher already has haste so it could attack regardless. The main question is whether Thought-Knot Seer's hand disruption (seeing and exiling a key card) would have been more impactful than Linebreaker's extra damage. With the opponent at 14 life and all lands tapped, the aggressive line is defensible, but TKS provides crucial information and disruption against an Aether Vial deck that will be vialing in creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Eldrazi Linebreaker using Cavern of Souls, Ancient Tomb, and Lotus Petal
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thought-Knot Seer using both Ancient Tombs (4 colorless mana) to strip a card from opponent's hand, getting critical information and disruption against their Aether Vial plan, then attack with Reality Smasher for 5

annotations.description: With opponent at 14 life and all their lands tapped, attacking with only Reality Smasher (8 damage) instead of all creatures leaves 3-5 points of damage on the table. Sending all attackers (Reality Smasher 8/5, Eldrazi Linebreaker 3/3, Glaring Fleshraker 2/2) forces opponent to make tough blocking decisions and maximizes pressure. White Orchid Phantom can only block one attacker, so most damage gets through.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Reality Smasher for 8 damage
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (All attack) to deal approximately 11-13 damage (minus one block), putting opponent to 1-3 life and likely setting up lethal next turn

annotations.description: Player chose to attack with only Reality Smasher instead of selecting 'All attack' which would have sent Eldrazi Linebreaker (which has haste) as well. Linebreaker as a 3/3 trampler could have dealt additional damage. Against an opponent at 14 life, the extra 3 damage (putting them to 5 instead of 8) is significant and could matter for closing out the game next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Reality Smasher (8/5 trample), dealing approximately 6 trample damage.
annotations.betterLine: Select 'All attack' to also send Eldrazi Linebreaker into combat, dealing approximately 3 additional damage and putting the opponent to 5 life instead of 8, creating a much more threatening lethal clock.

annotations.description: KimiK2 Vorthos declined to activate any abilities at the beginning of their turn. They have two Wastelands available and the opponent has two Ancient Tombs and a Cavern of Souls as their only lands (all tapped). Destroying an Ancient Tomb now (before the opponent untaps next turn) would significantly limit the opponent's mana production and ability to cast more Eldrazi threats. The opponent is at 12 life and already losing life to Ancient Tomb, so denying mana is critical. Additionally, the Aether Vial is at 3 counters but they have no creature cards in hand (only Aether Vial and Batterskull), so that activation wouldn't help. But Wasteland on Ancient Tomb is a clear play - the opponent's explosive mana base is enabling powerful Eldrazi, and with Eye of Ugin and City of Traitors already in the graveyard, destroying an Ancient Tomb would leave them with very limited mana going forward.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities, declining to use Wasteland.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland targeting one of the opponent's Ancient Tombs to severely constrain their mana production. This could be done at any point, but doing it proactively denies the opponent resources for their next turn.

annotations.description: Activated Aether Vial with no creature cards in hand, wasting the tap for the entire turn cycle. The activation resolves with nothing to put into play since the only card in hand is another Aether Vial (an artifact, not a creature).
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Aether Vial's ability to put a creature from hand onto the battlefield, but had no creature cards in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Should have held the Aether Vial untapped - either to potentially bluff or to preserve it for a future turn when a creature might be drawn. Passing without activating costs nothing.

annotations.description: Failed to block White Orchid Phantom (2/2) with Eldrazi Linebreaker (3/3), which would have killed the attacker while the Linebreaker survives. Instead took 2 unnecessary damage (12→10 life) and left the opponent's creature alive.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 2 damage from White Orchid Phantom
annotations.betterLine: Block White Orchid Phantom with Eldrazi Linebreaker (3/3 vs 2/2), killing the attacker while Linebreaker survives as 3/1

annotations.description: Casting Thought-Knot Seer pre-combat when lethal was already on board. White Orchid Phantom blocking only absorbs 2 damage with trample. Casting TKS first costs 2 life from Ancient Tomb (going to 8) and is unnecessary.

annotations.betterLine: Go directly to combat. Linebreaker trigger gives +3/+0 to Reality Smasher. Attack with all three creatures for 13 damage against opponent at 10 life with all permanents tapped - lethal without needing to cast anything.

annotations.betterLine: Wait until after draw step to see if a creature is drawn, then potentially activate Aether Vial. Or simply pass priority and focus on using Wastelands or other resources.

annotations.actionTaken: Activated Aether Vial with an empty hand, wasting the tap for no effect.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Wasteland to destroy one of Johnny's Ancient Tombs (denying mana and the creature-producing Glaring Fleshraker synergies), while keeping Batterskull equipped for lifelink blocking potential. Even at 1 life, a lifelink blocker is the best chance of survival.

annotations.description: At 1 life facing massive lethal on the opponent's board (Reality Smasher, Thought-Knot Seer, Glaring Fleshraker, Eldrazi Spawn), bouncing Batterskull to hand costs 3 mana but can't be replayed (costs 5) in time to matter. With 0 cards in hand and facing death next combat, this accomplishes nothing meaningful.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Batterskull's bounce ability to return it to hand, spending 3 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Use the two Wastelands to destroy the opponent's Ancient Tombs, denying future mana and at least providing some disruption. While likely still losing, mana denial is more impactful than holding a 5-mana equipment that can't be replayed in time.
